read_scope.notes: Read the complete 22-page frozen PDF, including the abstract, main text, references and Appendices A–G. Visually inspected every page, all five figures and Tables 1–10; reinspected page 7 at higher resolution. Consulted frozen paper.tex and specificity_results.tex to confirm wording, notation and figure captions. Technical appendices were assessed as optional depth. The abstract contains 152 whitespace-delimited words after normalizing TeX typography. SHA256 was independently computed from the supplied PDF. No prior drafts, other reviews, progress records or external research were consulted.

score_reasons.expression: Excellent, precise English with consistent distinctions among aligned response, total error, distributional proximity and perceptual fidelity. The explanations of shrinking GPT Image 2 contrasts and averaging Nano Banana 2 scenes (Section 5.4, page 9) connect quantities to their consequences particularly well. The abstract still compresses the central alignment-versus-mismatch distinction into technical labels before those labels have been explained; a localized wording change would improve its first reading.
score_reasons.structure: The progression from a concrete naming problem through experimental arms, interpretable feature families, score intuition, primary results and retrospective explanations is coherent. Sections 5.1–5.5 visibly separate the headline result, common response, painter-pair coverage, calibration and reference sensitivity. Technical identities, simulations and earlier cohorts remain optional appendices. The uncertainty paragraph in Section 4.3 would benefit from one additional paragraph boundary, but the main narrative does not require structural reconstruction.
score_reasons.new_reader_understanding: The three-step contrast explanation, measured Monet–Sisley lightness example, and idealized errors of 1, 0 and 1 make the central metric understandable without repository knowledge (Section 4.1, page 5). Table 1 interprets the measurements; Table 2 defines its scales and interval family; Table 3 explains calibration and the scene decomposition. Figure 1 makes all six prompt conditions inspectable, while Figures 2 and 3 distinguish projected geometry from all-feature pair scores. Remaining friction is localized to compressed abstract terminology and mapping several control intervals in Appendix C.1.
score_reasons.engagement: The paper sustains a concrete narrative: a visible name response can be mostly shared, aggregate alignment can conceal weak Monet–Sisley distinctions, and error orderings can change under explicit evaluation choices. The image matrix rewards inspection, the paired heatmaps reveal the weak distinctions immediately, and the numerical reversals in Section 5.4 explain why the methodological choices matter. There is no hype. Small gains in pace remain available by simplifying the abstract and separating uncertainty interpretation from procedural detail.

strengths: The opening Monet-versus-Sisley example explains why proximity to a painter collection is insufficient before introducing notation (page 1).
Section 4.1 uses an actual lightness gap and the no-distinction/exact/doubled-response examples to give the two scores intuitive anchors (page 5).
Figure 1 shows every condition for every model using a stated selection rule and explicitly distinguishes the historical reproductions from generator inputs and matched compositions (page 4).
The main results state both the positive aligned responses and the unresolved no-distinction benchmark, avoiding a misleading winner narrative (Section 5.1, pages 6–7).
Section 5.4 explains why shrinking contrasts changes GPT Image 2’s error and why scene averaging changes the Nano Banana 2–FLUX ordering; it explicitly limits both interpretations (page 9).
The source-correction discussion and Table 4 expose which interval conclusions change, including the retrospective status of the GPT Image 1 comparison (pages 9–10).

findings.issue: The central result is expressed through “positive reference alignment” and “total contrast error” before the abstract has explained what separates those two quantities. Centering has been introduced, but the reader still has to infer the difference between following a pattern and matching it accurately.
findings.reader_effect: A first-time reader can recover the general topic but may initially miss the paper’s most consequential result: a response in the reference direction can still have large overall mismatch.
findings.suggested_change: Replace that sentence with a plain-language equivalent, for example: “All models’ painter differences partly follow the reference pattern overall, yet none demonstrably reduces mismatch relative to making no painter distinctions.” Retain the measured-feature context and perceptual limitation already present. This is a sentence replacement and can remain within the 155-word abstract limit.

findings.issue: One paragraph combines the 21-endpoint family, Student/Bonferroni procedure, decision rule, descriptive absolute-error intervals, fixed-scene interpretation and repeat-independence limitations.
findings.reader_effect: The important distinction between how intervals are constructed and what their uncertainty represents is less easy to retain than the otherwise clear score definitions.
findings.suggested_change: Insert a paragraph break before “These approximations use variation across the 14 fixed briefs,” keeping the preceding sentences about the interval procedure together and the following interpretation/limitations together. No additional text or evidence is needed.

findings.issue: The three integrated-out sampling ranges and three original two-draw ranges are reported in separate prose sequences, requiring readers to remember the order of the three genuine-painting controls.
findings.reader_effect: Readers who choose this optional diagnostic must repeatedly map numbers back to pooled, class-stratified/pooled-target and class-target conditions to see what integrating out sampling changes.
findings.suggested_change: Replace the two range-list sentences with a compact three-row, two-result-column table using those three control labels and the existing six ranges. Keep the pooled SD comparison and caveat in prose, and use the replaced paragraph’s space so the manuscript stays within 22 pages.

summary: An excellent, self-contained account of a bounded digital-feature comparison. The main narrative makes the intervention, reference target, score meanings and limits readily understandable, and the figures support the findings. Remaining improvements are localized wording and presentation refinements; no new experiments or broader scientific claims are needed.
